name: Better Jobs Ontario (funded retraining for laid-off or long-unemployed people)
summary: Ontario grant of up to $28,000 (training of one year or less) or $35,000 (one to two years) covering tuition, books, transportation and an income-tested living allowance of up to $500 a week while an eligible laid-off or long-unemployed person retrains for an in-demand occupation. Applications go through an Employment Ontario provider.
what_you_do: With an Employment Ontario service provider you confirm you qualify, research an in-demand occupation and an approved training program, and complete a suitability assessment and application. If the ministry approves it, you attend the training with costs covered up to the caps, then look for work in the new field.
who_it_may_fit: You live in Ontario, were laid off and are not working (or are only in a temporary job to cover costs), or you have been unemployed for a long stretch in a low-income household, and you want funded training for a new occupation.
You receive EI, Ontario Works or ODSP; ontario.ca says these do not rule you out.
who_it_may_not_fit: You need income now: the living allowance is income-tested and only starts after approval, and one provider flyer estimates about 6-8 weeks of ministry processing after submission.
You are not a Canadian citizen or permanent resident (the Employment Ontario program overview lists residency and citizen/PR status).
You are employed and would have to quit; the program is built around people who were laid off or are unemployed.

summary: Short, paid, in-person work staffing voting places (and, for a few people, running a returning office) in the weeks around a municipal, provincial or federal election. name: Canada Training Credit (refundable tax credit for tuition, ages 26-65)
organization: Government of Canada - Canada Revenue Agency
summary: Refundable federal tax credit that repays up to half of eligible tuition and fees at a Canadian institution, up to your accumulated credit limit ($250 a year of room, lifetime $5,000) for people aged 26-65 with sufficient working income. Claimed on your tax return, not paid up front.
what_you_do: You check your Canada training credit limit on your notice of assessment, pay for an eligible course or occupational exam at a Canadian institution, and claim the lesser of your limit and 50% of the fees on line 45350 (Schedule 11) when you file. Room accumulates $250 a year while you meet the income tests.
who_it_may_fit: You are 26-65, resident in Canada all year, have at least about $12,000 of working income, and plan to pay for training at a Canadian college, university or exam body.
You want to lower the cost of a course that could lead to work; it combines with provincial funding such as Better Jobs Ontario where rules allow.
who_it_may_not_fit: You are under 26 or over 65 at year end, or you had no working income: your limit is zero and you cannot claim.
You need money before the course: the credit arrives with your tax refund after the year ends.
audience_restriction: Adults aged 26 to 65 at the end of the tax year

eligibility_notes: Resident in Canada throughout the year; file a return; aged at least 26 and under 66 at year end (CRA).
Annual $250 accumulation for 2026 requires at least $12,058 of working income (CRA); a net-income ceiling also applies (taxtips.ca cites $177,882 for 2025 income).

availability_evidence: CRA's Canada training credit page describes the credit as in force, with a $250 annual accumulation, the 2026 working-income threshold ($12,058), the 26-to-under-66 age window and claiming on line 45350 (search summary).

other: Fees paid to an eligible educational institution in Canada, or for an occupational, trade or professional exam
Tuition otherwise eligible for the tuition tax credit

conditions_notes: Funding mechanism for training, not work; the course you choose sets the schedule.

payment_terms: Refundable credit paid through your tax return for the year the fees were paid
economics_notes: Claim = lesser of your Canada training credit limit (accumulates $250/year to a lifetime $5,000) and 50% of eligible fees; institutions outside Canada do not qualify (CRA). Claiming also reduces the tuition amount available for the tuition tax credit.

risk_notes: Only refunds part of a course you have already paid for; it is not training funding.
barriers: Need enough working income to accumulate room
